bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI, building systems that learn from data and improve over time without explicit programming.
Core idea: systems learn patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Crucial in modern technology, used in image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, and autonomous vehicles.
Growth driven by large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised Learning, Unsupervised Learning, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: trains on labeled data to map inputs to known outputs (e.g., Regression, Classification).
Unsupervised Learning: trains on unlabeled data to find hidden patterns or structures (e.g., Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: agent learns by interacting with an environment to maximize cumulative rewards.
Model Training: feeding data to a model to learn patterns and adjust internal parameters.
Features and Labels: input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: data split for model training and performance evaluation on unseen data.
Overfitting: model learns training data too well, including noise, leading to poor performance on new data.
Underfitting: model is too simple and fails to capture important patterns in the data.
Linear Regression: for regression tasks, models linear relationships between variables.
Logistic Regression: for classification tasks, predicts probability of belonging to a class.
Decision Trees: non-linear model, splits data based on feature values, easy to interpret.
Random Forest: ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): finds optimal hyperplane to separate data points for classification.
Neural Networks: inspired by the human brain, learns complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment recommendations.
Finance: fraud detection, credit scoring, and algorithmic trading.
Marketing: customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, and targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: processing sensor data, decision-making, and safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: evaluate model performance using separate datasets.
Classification metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score.
Regression metrics: mean squared error (MSE), R-squared.
Cross-Validation: technique to ensure model generalizes well to unseen data.
Hyperparameter Tuning: optimizing model settings for optimal performance using techniques like grid search.
Data Quality and Quantity: models require large amounts of accurate, consistent, and complete data.
Interpretability: complex models (e.g., deep learning) are difficult to understand.
Bias in Data: models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: common issues affecting model generalization and performance.
Continuous evolution with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased integration into daily life across healthcare, education, entertainment, and transportation.
Growing importance of ethical considerations and responsible AI practices.
